subject: general
question: Akash sold an article at a loss of 17%. If he had bought the item at 5% less and had sold it for ₹310 more, then he would have gained 20%. Find the cost price (in ₹) of the article.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Initial Cost Price (CP₁)** = 100 units.

**Initial Selling Price (SP₁)** = 100 − 17 = 83 units.

**New Cost Price (CP₂)** = 100 − 5% = 95 units.

**New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 95 × (120 ÷ 100) = 114 units.

Difference in SP = 114 − 83 = 31 units ⇒ ₹310.

1 unit = ₹10 ∴ 100 units = 100 × 10 = ₹1,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Initial Loss = 17%, Reduction in CP = 5%, Extra SP = ₹310, New Profit = 20%.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 ± P/L%) ÷ 100 | Profit = SP − CP.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a87f863e9df22fef6d8dc4b6bc2c14ffa6785f5473c9d4ecd16c0017f2af9d9.png] 

⇒ Let original CP be **x**.

⇒ Original SP = 0.83x.

⇒ New CP = 0.95x.

⇒ New SP = 0.95x × 1.20 = 1.14x.

⇒ According to question: New SP − Original SP = 310.

⇒ 1.14x − 0.83x = 310 ⇒ 0.31x = 310 ⇒ x = 310 ÷ 0.31 = 1,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price relationship

When there are multiple changes in CP and SP, always assume the base **Cost Price** as 100 to simplify percentage calculations.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise. Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
